1.why: 26/28/29/32 form no run, no square, no derivational pair; nothing separates them, so this is a coin toss on the second-smallest.

2.why: 4.5% is the only non-integer among three round percentages (8/10/20), so it is the one value that looks computed rather than quoted.

3.why: 6/12 and 3/12 are unreduced (1/2, 1/4) and so read as distractors, but 5/12 and 7/12 are indistinguishable from each other.

4.why: Over 25ths the set is 17, 10, 8, 15 — two symmetric complement pairs (17+8, 10+15), so no option is singled out.

5.why: 10, 13, 16 is an arithmetic run of common difference 3 and 13 is its median, with 6 the lone outsider.

6.why: 29.5 is the derivational hub: 34.25 and 26.75 are 29.5 ± 4.75 and 69.5 is 29.5 + 40, so every other option is generated from it.

7.why: 2/15 is the only option whose denominator is the product of the others' denominators (3 x 5), the signature of the multiplied joint probability.

8.why: 30 and 40 are round tens that look like quoted givens, but 84 and 74 differ only by 10 and nothing distinguishes them structurally.

9.why: A complete 2x2 cross of numerators {3,7} against denominators {10,13} — perfectly symmetric, no option distinguished.

10.why: 4/16 is unreduced and drops out, but 5/16, 11/16 (complements) and 15/16 are all legal-looking; picking the complement half is arbitrary.

11.why: All four are binomial coefficients (210, 35, 15, 126); 210 is the largest and equals 35 x 6, a weak hub signal only.

12.why: 56.25% = 75%^2 and 43.75% is its complement, so both non-round values are computed; the two round ones are traps but the pair does not resolve.

13.why: 71, 74, 77 is an arithmetic run of difference 3 with 74 as its median, and 104 is the lone outlier.

14.why: 7/15 and 8/15 are complements and 1/3 = 5/15, while 12/25 is from a different denominator family; the complement pair itself is unresolved.

15.why: 7/20 = 1 - 2/5 - 1/4 exactly, i.e. the remainder after removing the two other simple options, which are the quoted givens.

16.why: 60 is the common multiple of 12 and 20 so it sits at the centre of the relations, while 27 relates to nothing; weak hub reasoning only.

17.why: 9 is the lone perfect square against 6, 11 and 14.

18.why: 3/8, 5/8, 7/8 is an arithmetic run of difference 2/8 with 5/8 its median, and 1/2 is the odd reduced outsider.

19.why: 27/125 is the only option that is an exact cube ratio, (3/5)^3, while 50/125 is merely unreduced 2/5.

20.why: 1/2, 2/3, 3/4, 5/6 are all simple n/(n+1) fractions with none singled out by size, form or reduction.

21.why: 3, 9 and 24 are all multiples of 3 and 11 is the lone prime outsider; 9 is the middle of the x3 pair, but the reasoning is thin.

22.why: 10, 15, 21 are triangular numbers over 36 and 15+21 = 36 while 10+26 = 36, giving two complement pairs and no unique option.

23.why: Over 20ths the options are 7, 8, 9, 10 — a complete arithmetic run, with 2/5 and 1/2 merely written reduced; the run has no single median.

24.why: 2/5 and 3/5 are the raw givens and 4/25 = (2/5)^2, so 21/25 = 1 - (2/5)^2 is the two-step value, but that lean is not a structural certainty.
